Debug checks and sanitizer wrappers for spad reset, delete, push, pop, alloc, trim, prepare, cancel, and publish.

# Purpose
`fd_spad` support code provides verification and debug wrappers for the `fd_spad` stack allocator. The [`fd_spad_verify`](<#fd_spad_verify>) function checks the allocator state, including the magic value, frame count, memory usage, and frame offset order. The file also defines debug entry points such as [`fd_spad_reset_debug`](<#fd_spad_reset_debug>), [`fd_spad_push_debug`](<#fd_spad_push_debug>), [`fd_spad_pop_debug`](<#fd_spad_pop_debug>), [`fd_spad_alloc_check`](<#fd_spad_alloc_check>), [`fd_spad_trim_debug`](<#fd_spad_trim_debug>), [`fd_spad_prepare_debug`](<#fd_spad_prepare_debug>), [`fd_spad_cancel_debug`](<#fd_spad_cancel_debug>), and [`fd_spad_publish_debug`](<#fd_spad_publish_debug>). These functions add state checks before they call the normal allocator implementation, and they stop execution with `FD_LOG_CRIT` when a caller uses the allocator in an invalid state.

The file also contains sanitizer-specific implementations for `FD_HAS_DEEPASAN` and `FD_HAS_MSAN`. These functions call the normal `fd_spad` implementation and then poison or unpoison memory regions with `fd_asan_poison`, `fd_asan_unpoison`, `fd_msan_poison`, and `fd_msan_unpoison`. This code keeps sanitizer state in sync with allocator state during reset, delete, push, pop, alloc, trim, prepare, cancel, and publish operations.
